hero.headline: One Licensed Contractor For The Whole Job
hero.subheadline: GARP Construction Group holds Florida certifications in general contracting, roofing, air conditioning and plumbing — so a Miami-Dade remodel, re-roof or build-out runs on one schedule, one contract and one point of contact.

promise_bar.text: GC, roofing, HVAC and plumbing in-house

promise_band.headline: We Don't Promise More Than We Can Deliver
promise_band.body: That sentence has been on our website since the company started, and it is the part we are most serious about. We take great pride in understanding our own capabilities — what we self-perform, what we sub out, and what a job will actually take. It is why the scope gets written down before anyone starts, and why we would rather lose a bid than win it on a number we cannot build to.

signature_system.headline: Four Licenses, One Contract
signature_system.intro: Most general contractors in South Florida hold a GC license and subcontract everything else. GARP holds four separate state certifications, which changes how a multi-trade job runs.

blocks.title: The trades that matter are in-house
blocks.body: General contracting (CGC1520370), roofing (CCC1329807), air conditioning (CAC1817062) and plumbing (CFC1429344) are all held by this company. When a re-roof turns up a rotted deck over a bathroom, the plumbing and the roofing are the same contract — not a change order and a two-week wait for another company's schedule.

blocks.title: Miami-Dade permitting is our job, not yours
blocks.body: We pull the permits, deal with the inspectors, and build to High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements. Unpermitted work in Miami-Dade catches up with a property at resale or at recertification, and we will not do it.

about_block.headline: A South Florida General Contractor Since 2012
about_block.body: GARP Construction Group Inc. is a general contractor based in Miami, serving Miami-Dade and Southeast Florida. Renovations, remodeling and maintenance are our specialties, with a focus on never sacrificing quality because of the size or scope of a project. Commercial or residential, we work closely with you to build what you actually asked for — and we manage projects throughout Southeast Florida from our Miami office.

seo_body.headline: General Contracting Built For South Florida Code
paragraphs: Miami-Dade is a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and it builds like one. Roof assemblies need product approvals, impact windows and doors need an NOA, and inspectors check for both. A contractor who works elsewhere in Florida and treats Miami-Dade as the same jurisdiction finds that out at inspection — with your project stopped.

We have built here since 2012 and hold the roofing, air conditioning and plumbing certifications alongside the general contractor's license. That means a re-roof, an AC changeout and a bathroom rough-in can run under one permit package and one schedule instead of three companies coordinating around each other.

faqs.q: What licenses does GARP Construction Group hold?
faqs.a: Four Florida state certifications: Certified General Contractor CGC1520370, Certified Roofing Contractor CCC1329807, Certified Air Conditioning Contractor CAC1817062, and Certified Plumbing Contractor CFC1429344. All four can be looked up on the Florida DBPR licence portal.

Yes. We prepare the permit package, pull it through Miami-Dade or the relevant municipality, meet the inspectors, and close the permit out. Unpermitted work causes real problems at resale and at building recertification, so we do not take jobs on the basis of skipping it.

faqs.q: Do you take commercial work as well as residential?
faqs.a: Both. We run residential remodels, re-roofs and pool builds alongside commercial build-outs and rooftop mechanical work, and have managed projects throughout Southeast Florida since 2012.
Yes. We come out to the property, look at the actual conditions, and give you a written scope and price at no charge. Call (305) 602-0400 or request one through the form on this site.

faqs.q: Do my new windows have to be impact rated?
faqs.a: In Miami-Dade, replacement windows and doors have to meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements and carry a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance — impact glazing or approved shutters. We only install units that carry the NOA the inspector will ask for.

faqs.q: How long does a re-roof take?
faqs.a: Most single-family re-roofs run a few days on the roof itself, but the permit and the inspection schedule usually drive the calendar more than the labour does. We quote the realistic permit timeline up front rather than after you have signed.
